paper_context.research_question: Does incorporating automatically-derived RST discourse structure via a recursive neural network with a novel (unnormalized) attention mechanism improve text categorization across multiple tasks and genres?
main_claims: Using discourse structure (RST) with a recursive neural network and an unnormalized attention mechanism improves text categorization accuracy on several tasks relative to prior work.

An UNLABELED variant (using tree structure without relation labels) often outperforms prior state-of-the-art across four of five datasets, while the FULL (relation-aware) model helps on very large datasets but can be overparameterized on smaller ones.

Discourse-derived benefits depend on the genre and on discourse parser quality: gains are smaller or negative when parser training domain diverges (e.g., legislative bills), and classifier accuracy degrades as discourse parser F1 declines.
The proposed unnormalized attention mechanism is empirically preferable to a normalized (softmax) variant for this discourse-composition setting.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper argues that automatically-produced RST discourse structure, when consumed by a recursive neural network with an unnormalized (elementwise sigmoid) attention mechanism, provides useful inductive bias for text categorization across several datasets and genres. The empirical claim is supported by multi-dataset experiments comparing full (relation-aware) and unlabeled (structure-only) variants to simpler baselines and published results. The reasoning chain links (a) discourse theory (nucleus/satellite importance) and a dependency transform, to (b) a recursive composition architecture with relation-specific matrices and attention, to (c) improved classification accuracy on most datasets. The paper also claims that (d) relation labels can be unnecessary or harmful on small datasets (UNLABELED often best), (e) unnormalized attention is preferable in this setting, and (f) parser quality and domain match are critical mediators of benefit. Overall coherence is good: model design is motivated by RST and empirically tested. Weaknesses in the argument arise from gaps in experimental control (potential uneven hyperparameter tuning, anonymized code link, limited cross-dataset attention comparisons, and possible non-comparability to prior work due to preprocessing/split differences). The causal claim that parser F1 directly controls classifier accuracy is plausible but not definitively isolated in the experiments presented.
logical_argument_graph: Node A: RST theory posits nucleus/satellite structure where nuclei are more central.
Node B: Automatic discourse parsers (DPLP) can produce RST trees for documents (trained on news WSJ).
Edge A->C: Use RST inductive bias to prioritize salient EDUs for categorization.
Node C: Convert RST constituency trees to dependency-style trees (Yoshida et al.) to supply tree structure for recursive models.
Node D: EDU representations are encoded via bidirectional LSTMs.
Node E: Propose recursive composition over dependency discourse trees with relation-specific matrices and an unnormalized attention α = σ(e_i^T W_α v_j). (FULL)
Node F: Propose UNLABELED variant removing relation-specific matrices to reduce parameters (vi = tanh(ei + Σ αij vj)).
Node G: Simpler baselines: ROOT (use root EDU only) and ADDITIVE (average EDUs; no discourse).
Edge D+E->H: Compose EDUs into document vector v_root used for classification (softmax).
Node H: Evaluate models on five datasets (Yelp, MFC, Debates, Movies, Bills).
Edge H->I: Empirical result: UNLABELED outperforms prior art on 4/5 datasets; FULL helps on the largest (Yelp).
Node I: Observed patterns: FULL overparameterized on small datasets; ADDITIVE sometimes competitive; ROOT poor.
Edge B->J: Parser domain/training size affects parser F1 on target genres.
Edge J->K: Degraded parser F1 leads to lower classifier accuracy (observational correlation from parser-size ablation).
Node L: Unnormalized attention compared to normalized softmax; demonstrated advantage (reported numeric example, limited scope).

Conclusion node M: Automatically-derived discourse structure can improve categorization when parser quality/genre match is adequate; UNLABELED can be preferable for small data; unnormalized attention is a useful architectural choice.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper proposes recursive neural composition over dependency-form RST parses, with a novel unnormalized (elementwise sigmoid) attention used to weight child contributions. Two parameter-reduced variants (UNLABELED, using tree structure without relation-specific matrices; and simpler baselines ROOT and ADDITIVE) are compared across five datasets of varying size and genre. Empirically, UNLABELED often matches or exceeds prior published baselines on four of five datasets; FULL (relation-aware) helps only on the largest dataset (Yelp) and appears overparameterized on smaller corpora. The authors analyze parser-quality effects by training the discourse parser on progressively smaller subsets of the RST treebank and report classifier accuracy falling with parser F1. They also present a limited comparison between their unnormalized attention and a normalized softmax variant (single-dataset number reported). The manuscript reports preprocessing and hyperparameter ranges, claims an implementation release (anonymous link), but omits precise parameter counts per variant, random seeds, and full artifacts. Key assumptions include adequacy of DPLP parses across genres, that unnormalized attention is stable and meaningful, and that hyperparameter selection was fair across variants and baselines.
logical_argument_graph: 1) RST discourse trees capture salience/nuclearity information useful for document-level tasks (theory and prior work).
2) Automatic discourse parses (DPLP) provide usable discourse trees for documents in several genres, after conversion to dependency-style trees.
3) A recursive neural network can compose EDU representations along this dependency tree to produce a document vector.
4) An unnormalized attention (sigmoid of inner product) applied per child better reflects RST's non-competitive salience than normalized attention.

5) Relation-specific composition (FULL) may add modeling power but substantially increases parameter count and risks overfitting on smaller datasets; removing relation parameters (UNLABELED) retains structural bias with fewer parameters.

6) Empirical results show UNLABELED outperforms prior published baselines on 4/5 datasets, FULL aids on the largest dataset only; parser quality (F1) correlates positively with classifier accuracy; normalized attention gives lower accuracy in an example comparison.
7) Therefore, automatically-derived discourse structure can be useful inductive bias for text categorization in many genres, conditional on parser quality and model capacity.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The manuscript adapts RST-style discourse structure (automatically produced by the DPLP parser) into a recursive neural network for document classification, introducing an unnormalized (elementwise sigmoid) attention mechanism for composing child nodes into parental representations. Two primary model families are evaluated: FULL (relation-aware, relation-specific composition matrices + unnormalized attention) and UNLABELED (tree-only + light-weight attention), with ROOT and ADDITIVE as simpler baselines. Empirical evaluation on five datasets (Yelp, MFC, Debates, Movies, Bills) shows that UNLABELED outperforms prior published baselines on four of five tasks; FULL only improves on the very large Yelp dataset and can overparameterize smaller corpora. The authors further study parser-quality sensitivity by training the discourse parser on subsets of the RST treebank (25/50/75/100%) and show classifier accuracy falling with parser F1. A comparison (limited) between unnormalized and normalized (softmax) attention is reported (single/dataset example: 70.3% vs 71.8%), motivating the unnormalized choice. Overall, the work is an incremental synthesis of prior ideas (discourse-informed weighting, recursive composition, neural attention) adapted to document categorization with empirical analyses emphasizing parameterization and parser-quality sensitivities.

Encode EDUs with BiLSTM -> vectors e_i (sentence/EDU encoder shared across variants)
Define recursive composition on dependency tree with child contributions weighted by attention -> full document vector v_root
Introduce unnormalized attention (sigmoid of bilinear) to avoid sibling competition (theoretical motivation from RST)

Degrading parser quality (fewer treebank examples) lowers parser F1 -> classifier accuracy drops -> parser quality mediates discourse benefit
Limited comparison indicates unnormalized attention outperforms normalized softmax on reported dataset(s) -> motivates attention design choice

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: Reconstructed reasoning: The paper starts from the theoretical claim that RST discourse structure encodes salience (nucleus/satellite, hierarchical organization) which can provide an inductive bias useful for text categorization. To operationalize this, the authors (1) obtain automatic RST parses via DPLP and convert constituency-style RST to a dependency-style tree (Yoshida-style transform); (2) encode EDUs with a Bi-LSTM sentence encoder; (3) recursively compose EDUs along the dependency-style discourse tree using a composition function that (in FULL) applies relation-specific linear transforms and an unnormalized, elementwise-sigmoid attention score per child (motivated by RST’s non-competitive salience), producing a document vector fed to a softmax classifier; (4) introduce simpler variants — UNLABELED (no relation matrices, only attention), ADDITIVE (flat average of EDUs), and ROOT (root EDU only) — to probe the contribution of structure, relation labels, and parameterization; (5) evaluate across five datasets spanning genres and dataset sizes, and compare to prior published baselines and ablations; (6) test parser-quality dependence by training DPLP on progressively smaller subsets of the RST treebank and re-parsing without re-tuning classifier hyperparameters; (7) compare normalized (softmax) vs. unnormalized attention in a limited set of experiments. The empirical pattern reported: UNLABELED often matches or exceeds prior state-of-the-art (4/5 datasets), FULL helps on the very large Yelp dataset but appears overparameterized on smaller corpora, parser quality and genre mismatch (e.g., legislative bills) reduce or reverse gains, and an unnormalized attention variant gave a modest improvement (reported explicitly for Yelp). The paper argues that (a) explicit discourse structure — even when produced automatically from a parser trained on news — can provide useful inductive bias for some categorization tasks; (b) relation labels are not uniformly beneficial and can harm on small datasets due to overparameterization; (c) attention normalization assumptions from other tasks may not be appropriate for discourse composition; and (d) improvements in discourse parsing would likely expand the utility of the approach. Key methodological caveats in the manuscript (and which affect the strength of causal claims) include: lack of full parameter-count transparency per variant in the main text, anonymized/placeholder implementation link, non-repetition of hyperparameter search in parser-degradation experiments, dataset-dependent embedding regimes (pretrained GloVe vs. learned embeddings), and limited cross-dataset evidence for the normalized vs. unnormalized attention claim.
logical_argument_graph: G1: RST discourse trees encode sentence/spans salience (nucleus/satellite) => useful inductive bias for selecting/weighting content for categorization.
G2: Automatic discourse parsing (DPLP) + dependency transformation yields usable tree structures for downstream neural composition (assumes reasonable parser accuracy / convertibility).
G3: Represent EDUs with BiLSTM vectors; recursively compose up the dependency tree to obtain a document vector (composition function distinguishes parent, children).
G4: Use per-child attention scores; unnormalized (sigmoid) attention is motivated by RST theory (no competition among siblings) and by potential numerical/representational benefits in composition.
G5: Variants (UNLABELED vs FULL vs ADDITIVE vs ROOT) isolate the roles of relation labels, tree structure, and trivial root selection; parameter counts control overfitting risk.
G6: Empirical evaluation across 5 datasets shows UNLABELED outperforming prior work on 4/5 (FULL best on largest dataset only), supporting claims G1–G5 under the tested conditions.
G7: Controlled parser-quality degradation (less RST training data) reduces parser F1 and correlates with reduced classifier accuracy => evidence that parser quality mediates gains.
G8: Therefore, the approach is useful in many genres but sensitive to parser-domain mismatch and parameterization; unnormalized attention is preferred in at least some conditions.
G9: Implication: improving discourse parsing and careful model-sizing would enlarge practical applicability of discourse-based inductive bias for categorization.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper argues that automatically-produced RST discourse structure, consumed via a recursive neural network with an unnormalized (elementwise sigmoid) attention mechanism, provides a useful inductive bias for document classification. The architecture (FULL) composes EDUs along a dependency-form discourse tree using relation-specific composition matrices and unnormalized attention; a parameter-reduced UNLABELED variant omits relation matrices and often performs best; ROOT and ADDITIVE baselines probe trivial explanations. Empirically, UNLABELED outperforms previously published baselines on four of five datasets (Yelp, MFC, Debates, Movies) while FULL only helps on the largest dataset (Yelp). The authors present qualitative attention visualizations and an experiment degrading the discourse parser (DPLP) by training it with less data; classifier accuracy falls with parser F1. They also report a limited comparison showing unnormalized attention yielding higher accuracy than a normalized (softmax) variant on at least Yelp. Strengths include coherent mapping from RST theory to architecture, multi-genre evaluation, and explicit ablations. Key concerns that weaken causal or general claims are: potential unfairness / non-comparability to prior baselines (relying on published numbers), missing reproducibility detail (anonymized link, missing seeds and per-variant parameter counts), confounding in the parser-degradation experiment (hyperparameters not re-tuned per parser condition), and limited cross-dataset evidence for the unnormalized attention claim. Introduce unnormalized, elementwise-sigmoid attention to avoid competition among siblings (motivated by RST).
Define lighter-weight variants: UNLABELED (no relation matrices), ADDITIVE (flat sum), ROOT (root EDU only) to isolate where benefits come from.

concerns.description: When assessing the impact of parser quality (training DPLP on reduced treebank sizes), the authors did not repeat classifier hyperparameter search per parser condition; observed classifier accuracy drops may conflate parser quality effects with suboptimal hyperparameters or EDU segmentation changes.
evidence: Section 6: 'We did not repeat the hyperparameter search. In Figure 4, we plot accuracy of the classifier against the F1 performance of the discourse parser.'
Shared analysis and prior-stage reviewers note this confound.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Re-run the parser-degradation experiments while performing hyperparameter selection (same grid) for the classifier separately for each parser condition; additionally report EDU segmentation statistics (counts, average length) under each parser condition.

concerns.title: Limited evidence for unnormalized attention generality
concerns.description: The empirical superiority of the unnormalized (sigmoid) attention over normalized (softmax) is supported by a single reported comparison (70.3 vs 71.8 on Yelp); it's unclear whether this holds across datasets and hyperparameter settings, and whether parameterization/regularization was matched.
evidence: Section 6: presents a single number 'This variant of the FULL model achieves 70.3% accuracy' vs FULL's 71.8% on Yelp.
No cross-dataset comparison or statistical testing reported for this contrast.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Evaluate normalized vs unnormalized attention across all datasets with matched hyperparameter tuning, matched parameter counts (or controlled capacity), and report statistical significance and training dynamics (stability, gradient norms).

concerns.title: Reproducibility gaps: anonymized link and missing details
concerns.description: The implementation link is anonymized and crucial artifacts are not enumerated (random seeds, per-experiment hyperparameters, exact parameter counts per variant, trained checkpoints), hampering reproducibility and precise attribution of gains.
evidence: Section 4: 'Our implementation is available at http:// anonymous.link.'
Shared analysis notes missing parameter counts, seeds, and exact configs per run.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide the full repository (code + instructions), exact experiment configs (hyperparameters chosen per dataset and variant), random seeds, and parameter counts (number of parameters per model/variant). If anonymization is required for review, include a supplementary non-anonymized artifact for reproducibility check with the chairs or an embargoed link.

concerns.title: Possible confound from embedding regimes across datasets
concerns.description: The authors use pretrained GloVe for small datasets and randomly-initialized trainable embeddings for large datasets; embedding initialization may interact with model variants and could partially explain differences across datasets or between FULL and UNLABELED.
evidence: Section 4: 'In cases where there are 10,000 or fewer training examples, we used pretrained GloVe; for larger datasets, we randomly initialize word embeddings and train them alongside other model parameters.'
FULL helps on Yelp (large dataset with randomly-initialized embeddings) while UNLABELED helps on smaller datasets (pretrained embeddings).
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Run controlled experiments where embedding initialization is held constant across variants (e.g., both pretrained+finetune and random-init+train across sample datasets), and report whether relative gains persist.

comparable_works.relevance: Primary baseline on Yelp (hierarchical attention networks using normalized attention on sentences).
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Shares idea of attention over textual units but HAN uses a flat sentence-level structure with normalized attention; current paper introduces discourse tree structure and unnormalized attention.

comparable_works.relevance: Prior work applying discourse-based, hand-crafted weighting schemes for sentiment analysis (discourse dependency tree, unlabeled weighting).
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Both use discourse trees to weight sentences; current paper learns attention weights and composes recursively rather than using hand-crafted weights.

comparable_works.relevance: The discourse parser used to produce RST parses for input to the model.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: DPLP provides automatic RST parsing; current paper depends on its output and studies sensitivity to its quality.

comparable_works.relevance: Method for transforming constituency-style RST to dependency-style trees used here.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Authors follow Yoshida's transform; current work composes over the resulting dependency tree.

uncertainty_flags: Baseline comparisons use published numbers; matching preprocessing/splits is not guaranteed—this creates uncertainty about the magnitude and existence of reported advantages.

Parser-degradation experiment did not re-tune classifier hyperparameters per parser condition; observed accuracy decline may conflate parser quality with hyperparameter mismatch and segmentation differences.
The attention normalization claim is supported by a single reported comparison (Yelp); its cross-dataset generality is uncertain.
Reproducibility artifacts (code link, seeds, parameter counts, per-run hyperparameters) are missing or anonymized, limiting independent verification.
alternative_interpretations: Some of the UNLABELED advantage could stem from better regularization due to fewer parameters rather than from tree structure per se; controlling for parameter count could shift relative performance.

Improvements attributed to discourse structure might instead be partially caused by preprocessing choices (vocabulary cutoff to map ~5% tokens to UNK) or embedding regimes (pretrained vs randomly initialized) interacting with dataset sizes.
The parser-degradation effect might reflect changes in EDU segmentation (number and length of EDUs) altering input granularity for the classifier, not only parser label quality.
transparency_notes: The public implementation link is anonymized; make full code, configs, seeds, and trained checkpoints available to allow reproduction.
Parameter counts per model/variant are discussed qualitatively ('nearly 20 times') but should be reported precisely (number of parameters, layer sizes) per dataset and variant.
Report the exact hyperparameter choices selected per dataset and per variant (word dims, LSTM dims, optimizer, learning rate, dropout) in supplementary material or repository.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: The combination of dependency-transformed RST, recursive neural composition with relation-specific matrices, and an unnormalized attention mechanism is not a direct copy of a single prior method; sparse precedent suggests potential innovation, but novelty does not guarantee empirical robustness—rigorous controlled experiments are needed.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If discourse parser accuracy is high on the target genre (or parser is adapted to the genre), then the recursive discourse composition should yield consistent gains.
If relation labels are reliably predicted and datasets are large enough to support relation-specific parameters, FULL should outperform UNLABELED.

If unnormalized attention remains numerically stable across documents with highly variable branching factors and is tuned to avoid scale issues, the intended non-competitive salience behavior could translate into better performance.

novelty_lenses.rationale: The work combines known components—automatic RST parsing, dependency transform, recursive composition, attention—in a new configuration (unnormalized attention + dependency RST composition) and performs novel empirical analyses (parser-degradation). This constitutes meaningful incremental synthesis rather than a radical paradigm shift.
evidence: Sections 2-3 position paper relative to prior methods (Bhatia et al., Yang et al.).
Prior-stage digest labels it as an incremental synthesis.
uncertainty_flags: Degree of novelty hinges on the originality of the unnormalized attention idea in discourse composition; limited cross-dataset empirical support leaves its broad novelty impact uncertain.

novelty_lenses.rationale: If the unnormalized attention + recursive RST composition reliably improves classification across many genres and parser improvements come, this approach could shift emphasis toward discourse-aware document encoders. However, currently evidence is limited by reproducibility gaps and confounds, so disruptive impact is conditional on stronger validation.
evidence: Observed UNLABELED wins on multiple datasets indicate potential.
Parser-quality sensitivity analysis suggests direction for future improvements in discourse parsing to unlock more gains.
uncertainty_flags: Current limitations in experimental control and reporting make it premature to claim broad disruptive impact.

confidence_interval.rationale: I have high confidence in the internal coherence of the paper's argument and the reported within-manuscript evidence (tables/figures). However, due to methodological confounds noted (baseline comparability, missing reproducibility artifacts, parser-degradation untuned), generalization and causal strength are substantially uncertain. The interval reflects moderate-to-high confidence that the reported experimental pattern (UNLABELED wins, FULL helps for large data, parser quality matters) is real within the manuscript's pipeline, but lower confidence that these results would generalize under fully controlled reproduction and broader datasets.

consensus_findings: The manuscript presents a coherent theory-driven architecture that composes EDU representations along dependency-form RST trees using an elementwise-sigmoid (unnormalized) attention, with clearly defined variants: FULL (relation-aware), UNLABELED (structure-only), ADDITIVE (flat), and ROOT (single EDU).

The UNLABELED variant (tree structure without relation-specific matrices) shows the most consistent empirical gains within the authors' experimental pipeline, outperforming published baselines on four of the five reported datasets in Table 2.
FULL (relation-aware) can improve performance on large datasets but risks overparameterization and worse performance on smaller datasets unless parameterization is controlled.

The authors identify and empirically illustrate sensitivity of downstream classifier accuracy to discourse parser quality: when the upstream parser is degraded (trained on less RST treebank data), parser F1 falls and classifier accuracy tends to decline in the reported pipeline.

ROOT baseline (single EDU) performs poorly; ADDITIVE (flat sum/average of EDUs) is competitive on some datasets, indicating that composition and weighting mechanisms (and encoder capacity) materially affect outcomes.

Reproducibility and reporting gaps exist in the manuscript: the implementation link is anonymized/placeholder, exact parameter counts per variant, random seeds, and per-experiment hyperparameter selections are not fully enumerated in the paper.
disagreements: Scope/generalizability of the unnormalized-attention advantage: reviewers agree the architecture is plausible and the Yelp example favors unnormalized attention, but disagree about whether the provided evidence (mostly a single-dataset numeric example) suffices to claim general empirical preferability across datasets.

Causal strength of the parser-quality -> classifier-accuracy relationship: all reviewers observe correlation in the reported experiments, but several raise that the parser-degradation study did not repeat classifier hyperparameter tuning per parser condition, producing disagreement about whether the observed effect is primarily due to parser quality or partly due to untuned classifier settings and changing EDU segmentation.

Interpretation of UNLABELED's superiority: some reviewers interpret UNLABELED's wins as evidence that relation labels add little value for small datasets, while others caution that reduced parameter count and embedding-initialization regimes may explain the advantage; thus there is a controlled disagreement between attributing gains to structural signal vs capacity/regularization differences.

Fairness of comparisons to prior work: reviewers agree the comparisons are informative but disagree about how directly comparable they are, because the paper reports published baseline numbers rather than re-running baselines under an identical preprocessing and split pipeline; some see the reported wins as plausible, others treat them as potentially confounded.
uncertainty_hotspots: Attention-normalization generality: lack of cross-dataset, parameter-matched comparisons and stability analyses (multiple seeds/statistics) for unnormalized vs normalized attention.

Parser-degradation confound: hyperparameter re-tuning was not performed after re-parsing; uncertainty whether classifier drops are due to parser F1, changed EDU counts/segmentations, or mis-tuned classifier hyperparameters.

Parameter-count / capacity effects: exact numbers not provided; 'nearly 20x' claim is qualitative. Uncertainty whether UNLABELED benefits are due to lower capacity rather than absence of relation labels.

Baseline comparability / preprocessing differences: reported prior-work numbers may use different tokenization, vocabulary, and splits; uncertain how much of the reported improvement remains under truly matched experimental conditions.
Reproducibility artifacts: anonymized implementation link and missing seeds/configs prevent independent replication; uncertainty about whether reported configurations can be precisely reproduced.

EDU segmentation and dependency transform effects: limited reporting on EDU counts/length distributions and on whether the constituency-to-dependency transform preserves crucial signals; uncertainty about how segmentation interacts with results, particularly for domain-distant corpora (e.g., bills).
model_diversity_effects: Model variants (FULL vs UNLABELED vs ADDITIVE vs ROOT) produce consistent role-specific effects: UNLABELED tends to balance expressivity and parameter economy and performs well on small-to-medium datasets; FULL increases expressivity via relation-specific matrices but substantially increases parameter count, yielding benefits primarily on large datasets and risks overfitting on small ones.

ADDITIVE demonstrates that a strong EDU encoder plus simple aggregation can be competitive; this suggests part of the gains attributed to discourse structure may be recoverable via encoder improvements or simpler weighting strategies in some domains.

Choice of attention normalization interacts with tree-structured composition dynamics: unnormalized attention permits multiple children to be salient independently (theoretically aligned with RST), while normalized attention enforces competition among siblings; empirical effects appear dataset-dependent and sensitive to implementation/tuning.

Upstream model diversity (parser quality and segmentation behavior) propagates downstream: degraded parser outputs (lower F1, different segmentation) systematically change input distributions to the recursive model, altering optimal hyperparameters and potentially model ranking.

Embedding-regime diversity (pretrained GloVe for small datasets vs randomly-initialized trainable embeddings for large datasets) may interact with model variants, influencing which variant generalizes better in each dataset.
meta_review.editor_guidance: Position the editor as the decision centralizer: request targeted, reproducibility-focused rebuttal experiments from the authors before relying on these empirical claims for strong conclusions. Specifically ask authors to (a) release the non-anonymized codebase and configuration artifacts (or provide an embargoed reproducibility package to the chairs) including seeds, per-experiment hyperparameters, and parameter counts; (b) re-run or report controlled ablations that disentangle parameter-count/capacity effects from relation-label utility (for example, FULL with constrained parameter budget or UNLABELED with matched capacity); (c) repeat the parser-degradation experiments while re-tuning classifier hyperparameters per parser condition and report EDU segmentation statistics per condition (mean/median EDUs per document, length distributions); (d) perform attention-normalization comparisons across all datasets under matched parameter counts and hyperparameter search, including variance over multiple random restarts; and (e) either re-run strong baselines in the same preprocessing/split pipeline or clearly document mismatches and, where feasible, re-evaluate at least the main baselines under identical conditions. Keep decisions contingent on the authors addressing these reproducibility and confound-removal tasks. Avoid collapsing reviewer disagreement into a single averaged verdict; instead, use the additional experiments to resolve the principal uncertainties (attention generality, parser-quality causality, parameterization confounds, and baseline comparability).
meta_review.author_guidance: To strengthen claims and resolve controlled disagreements, provide the following targeted deliverables and analyses: (1) Release the full code, preprocessing scripts, dataset split definitions, final trained checkpoints (or training scripts with seeds), and a reproducibility README. If anonymization for review persists, submit an embargoed artifact to the chairs. (2) Tabulate exact parameter counts for each model component and for each variant (FULL, UNLABELED, ADDITIVE, ROOT) used in each dataset/run. (3) Run capacity-controlled experiments: match FULL and UNLABELED parameter budgets (e.g., via low-rank relation matrices, parameter sharing, or reducing FULL dimensions) and report whether relation labels still help. (4) Repeat the parser-degradation experiments while performing the same hyperparameter selection procedure separately for each parser condition; report both tuned and untuned results and provide EDU segmentation statistics (EDU counts per document, length distributions) per condition. (5) Systematically compare unnormalized vs normalized attention across all datasets, ensuring matched parameter counts and hyperparameter searches, and report mean ± standard deviation across multiple random seeds. (6) Re-evaluate at least the strongest prior baselines (e.g., HAN / Yang et al.) under the identical preprocessing and data splits used in your experiments, or clearly document and quantify any differences between your pipeline and prior published setups. (7) Add a reproducibility appendix listing final hyperparameters per dataset/variant, random seeds, early-stopping criteria, and training curves. These steps will reduce the main sources of uncertainty and let readers and reviewers judge the robustness and generality of the central claims.
transparency_report: Available in manuscript: theoretical motivation, model equations, variant definitions, datasets used, hyperparameter search ranges, training regimes (optimizer, dropout, clipping), and qualitative attention visualizations.
Partially available / anonymized: implementation link is stated but anonymized (placeholder), preventing direct access to code and artifacts during review.

Missing from manuscript: exact parameter counts per model variant and per dataset, final selected hyperparameter values per reported result, random seeds and number of random restarts, trained checkpoints or deterministic reproduction scripts, and detailed preprocessing/tokenization scripts for every dataset.

Reported but needing strengthening: parser-degradation experiment protocol is described (training DPLP on 25/50/75/100% of treebank), but hyperparameter re-selection for classifier was not done per condition (explicitly stated).

Suggested additions for transparency: (a) a table with parameter counts and selected hyperparameters per dataset/variant; (b) a reproducibility package (code + configs + seeds + example commands); (c) reports of mean ± std over multiple runs for main metrics; (d) EDU segmentation statistics per dataset and per parser condition; (e) explicit mapping documenting any preprocessing differences relative to prior baselines used for comparison.
epistemic_limits: The synthesis and reviewers' analyses rest on reported results within the authors' experimental pipeline; independent replication has not been demonstrated due to anonymized code link and missing artifacts. Causal inferences (e.g., parser F1 causes classifier accuracy decline, or unnormalized attention is generally superior) are limited because key potential confounds were not fully controlled: classifier hyperparameters were not re-tuned after changing parser outputs, parameter-count differences between variants were not precisely reported or controlled, and baseline comparisons rely on published numbers that may not match the paper's preprocessing/splits. Moreover, evidence for some claims (unnormalized attention advantage, generality of UNLABELED superiority) is currently narrow in scope (single-dataset examples or five datasets only). Treat reported correlations as plausible within the authors' pipeline but epistemically uncertain until the requested controlled re-runs, capacity-matching ablations, cross-dataset attention analyses, and reproducibility artifacts are supplied. Finally, absence of public artifacts prevents assessment of numerical stability, optimization sensitivity, and variance across random seeds, which are necessary to generalize from the reported findings to broader claims about discourse-informed neural document encoders.

human_facing_meta_review.summary: This manuscript proposes recursive neural composition over dependency-form RST discourse trees with an elementwise-sigmoid (unnormalized) attention mechanism and evaluates several variants (FULL with relation-specific matrices, UNLABELED without relation matrices, ADDITIVE, ROOT) on five datasets spanning genres and sizes. Within the authors' experimental pipeline, the UNLABELED variant often yields the strongest results (outperforming published baselines on four of five datasets), FULL helps on the largest dataset but can be overparameterized on smaller ones, and downstream gains degrade when the upstream discourse parser is weakened. The unnormalized attention is theoretically motivated by RST (no sibling competition) and shown to outperform a normalized softmax variant in a limited reported comparison.
strengths: Theory-driven architecture: model design links RST concepts (nucleus/satellite, non-competitive salience) to a concrete recursive composition and an elementwise-sigmoid attention formulation.
Well-structured ablation suite: FULL, UNLABELED, ADDITIVE, and ROOT isolate the roles of relation labels, tree structure, and trivial baselines.
Multi-genre empirical evaluation: experiments span five datasets (Yelp, MFC, Debates, Movies, Bills), enabling analysis of dataset-size and domain sensitivity (e.g., bills domain mismatch).
Explicit parser-quality probe: the authors attempt to quantify how degrading the discourse parser (training on smaller treebank subsets) affects downstream classifier accuracy.
limitations: Reproducibility gaps: the implementation link is anonymized/placeholder; exact parameter counts per variant, the final chosen hyperparameters per experiment, random seeds, number of random restarts and trained checkpoints are not provided, preventing independent replication.

Confounded parser-degradation study: when re-parsing with weaker parser models the classifier hyperparameter tuning was not repeated per parser condition; therefore observed classifier accuracy declines may conflate parser-quality effects with mis-tuned classifier hyperparameters and changes in EDU segmentation.

Comparability to published baselines is uncertain: the paper juxtaposes published numbers rather than re-running baselines under identical preprocessing and splits, leaving open whether reported improvements are fully apples-to-apples.

Limited evidence for unnormalized-attention generality: the normalized-vs-unnormalized attention comparison is reported only in a narrow scope (single-dataset numeric example) without matched parameter-count/hyperparameter parity and without variance estimates.
open_questions: Please provide exact parameter counts (total and per major component) for each model variant (FULL, UNLABELED, ADDITIVE, ROOT) used in each dataset/run. How many parameters make up the 'nearly 20x' claim?

Can the parser-degradation experiments be re-run with hyperparameter selection repeated for the classifier at each parser-training-size condition (25/50/75/100%) and with EDU segmentation statistics (mean/median EDUs per document, length distributions) reported, to separate parser-F1 effects from tuning/segmentation effects?

Please report systematic normalized vs. unnormalized attention comparisons across all datasets with matched parameter budgets and hyperparameter searches, including mean ± standard deviation across multiple random seeds. Do the unnormalized advantages persist under these controls?

For baseline comparability: can the strongest prior baselines (e.g., Hierarchical Attention Network / Yang et al. 2016) be re-run under the same preprocessing and splits used here, or can the authors document precise preprocessing/split differences and sensitivity to them?

Provide the non-anonymized code repository or an embargoed reproducibility package (code, preprocessing scripts, training commands, selected hyperparameters, random seeds, and at least one trained checkpoint). If immediate release is impossible, supply a reproducibility appendix with final hyperparameters and parameter counts.

How sensitive are results to the embedding regime choice (pretrained GloVe for small datasets vs random-init+train for large ones)? Please run a controlled ablation holding embedding initialization constant for representative datasets.
consensus_snapshot: The architectural idea of composing over discourse-derived dependency trees with an RST-motivated unnormalized attention is conceptually coherent and well-motivated.
Within the authors' pipeline, UNLABELED often performs best across the reported datasets, while FULL can overparameterize small datasets and helps primarily on large data.
Downstream performance depends on upstream discourse parser quality and genre match: degraded parser F1 correlates with reduced classifier accuracy in the reported experiments.
Reproducibility and reporting need strengthening (code, seeds, exact hyperparameters, parameter counts, and matched-baseline re-runs) before firm generalization can be accepted.
disagreement_snapshot: Whether UNLABELED's superiority is primarily due to tree-structure signal (absence of relation labels) or largely attributable to lower parameter count / regularization advantage—reviewers differ; controlled capacity-matching ablations are needed.
Generality of the unnormalized-attention claim: some reviewers find the Yelp example suggestive, others require cross-dataset, parameter-matched evidence before accepting a general claim.

Causal interpretation of parser F1 -> classifier accuracy: reviewers agree on correlation in the presented pipeline but disagree about causal strength because classifier hyperparameters were not re-tuned after changing parses.
uncertainty_snapshot: Parser-degradation causal attribution is uncertain without per-condition hyperparameter re-tuning and EDU-segmentation diagnostics.
Effect sizes and statistical stability are uncertain because results are reported without mean±std over multiple random restarts or confidence intervals.
Comparative advantage versus prior work is uncertain due to potential preprocessing/split mismatches; re-running baselines under identical pipelines would clarify.
Numerical stability and behavior of unnormalized attention across documents with varying branching factors (child counts) is not fully characterized.

human_facing_meta_review.comments:
Summary:
The paper develops a recursive neural model that composes EDU vectors along dependency-form RST trees using a theoretically-motivated elementwise-sigmoid (unnormalized) attention. Evaluated across five datasets and several ablations, the UNLABELED (structure-only) variant often yields the best results in the authors' pipeline; FULL (relation-aware) helps on the largest dataset but can overparameterize small datasets; downstream gains fall when the upstream discourse parser is degraded.

Strengths:
- Strong theory-to-architecture mapping (RST → dependency transform → unnormalized attention).
- Thoughtful ablations (FULL/UNLABELED/ADDITIVE/ROOT) clarify where benefits may arise.
- Reasonably broad empirical scope across multiple genres and dataset sizes.
- Explicit attempt to probe parser-quality sensitivity.

Limitations:
- Missing reproducibility artifacts (anonymized repo link, missing seeds, missing per-experiment hyperparameters and parameter-count tables) hinder independent verification.
- Parser-degradation experiment did not re-tune classifier hyperparameters per parser condition; observed accuracy drops may conflate parser-quality effects with hyperparameter/segmentation confounds.
- Comparisons to published baselines are potentially non-apples-to-apples because baselines were not re-run under identical preprocessing and splits.
- The unnormalized vs normalized attention claim is supported by limited cross-dataset evidence and lacks parameter-matched comparisons and variance estimates.

Open Questions:
- Provide exact parameter counts per model variant and dataset. How was the ~20x parameter claim computed and which components dominate the count? 
- Can the parser-degradation runs be repeated with full hyperparameter search per condition, and can EDU segmentation statistics be reported (counts and length distributions) to see what changed when the parser was weakened? 
- Do unnormalized-attention advantages persist when normalized and unnormalized variants are given matched parameter budgets and matched hyperparameter search across all datasets, with mean±std over multiple seeds reported? 
- Can at least the main prior baselines (e.g., HAN / Yang et al.) be re-run in the same preprocessing and split pipeline, or can you document precise preprocessing/split differences and report sensitivity? 
- Please release the full non-anonymized code and a reproducibility appendix listing hyperparameters and seeds; if immediate public release is impossible, provide an embargoed artifact to the chairs.

Transparency:
Manuscript provides clear model equations, datasets, hyperparameter search ranges, and qualitative examples. Missing are concrete artifacts required for independent replication: non-anonymized code, exact per-experiment hyperparameters and parameter counts, random seeds and number of restarts, trained checkpoints, and per-dataset preprocessing/tokenization scripts. The parser-degradation methodology is described but must be rerun with per-condition tuning and segmentation diagnostics to support causal claims about parser F1 mediating classifier performance.

confidence_interval.rationale: Lower bound reflects uncertainty introduced by missing reproducibility artifacts, hyperparameter/tuning confounds in the parser-degradation experiments, and limited cross-dataset evidence for attention normalization claims. Upper bound reflects the internal coherence of the design, plausibility of the theory-to-architecture mapping, and the consistency of reported empirical patterns within the authors' pipeline. The interval expresses moderate-to-high confidence in the manuscript's conceptual contribution and in the reported pipeline's internal results, but only moderate confidence that the empirical claims will generalize under stricter, reproducible controls.
